answer.label: A later report — not authenticated Spurgeon wording
answer.sourceLine: The Spurgeon Library rejects this compact sentence as an authenticated Spurgeon quotation. It identifies a later attributed retelling in W.A.Criswell’s 1955 sermon and an unsourced 1992 biography. Criswell’s transcript is evidence that the anecdote circulated, not an original Spurgeon source. Its creator remains unidentified.

context.heading: The setting behind the words
lead: The beeline story became part of later descriptions of Spurgeon’s preaching. The library distinguishes it from a real sermon in which Spurgeon recounts a Welsh minister’s road-to-Christ illustration. Both concern Christ-centered preaching, but they are separate stories with different sourcing. Spurgeon Library source criticism ↗
